newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iran denies role in Mubarak assassination attempt.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies role in Mubarak assassination attempt.

text.p: Iran has denied Egyptian accusations it was involved in the assassination attempt on Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Ethiopia last year.

The official Iranian news agency IRNA on Saturday quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi as saying Iran "as a basic and unchanging principle has always condemned resorting to acts of terrorism".
IRNA said Mohammadi was speaking in the Ugandan capital Kampala on Friday night, one of six African states that Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani is visiting.
It said Mohammadi was reacting to comments made on Thursday by Osama el-Baz, senior political adviser to Mubarak, that Iran was involved in the assassination attempt.
"An Egyptian terrorist group carried out this attempt with the help of the Sudanese and also Iranian governments," El-Baz told the Qatar News Agency.

Egypt has accused Sudan of helping the gunmen who tried to kill Mubarak in Addis Ababa in June 1995. Sudan denies this. El-Baz's remarks marked the first time an Egyptian official has accused Iran of involvement in the assassination attempt.

"The Islamic republic of Iran regards the statement...as a sign of the Egyptian regime's concern over close relations among Islamic countries and an attempt to shift the domestic problems of Egypt to foreign countries," Mohammadi said.

Egypt, locked in a low-level guerrilla war with Moslem militants seeking to oust Mubarak and impose an Islamic state, has often accused Iran of trying to export its 1979 Islamic revolution to other regional states. Iran has denied the charge.
